blueprint.name: Recruitment Test
blueprint.source: UPSC APFC Recruitment Test: single 2-hour objective paper, 160 questions, 300 marks, -1/3 negative. Syllabus areas mapped to bank sections; Industrial Relations and Accountancy have no reviewed-bank source and are model-filled, labelled as such.

questions.text: A vessel contains 100 litres of pure milk. 10 litres of milk is taken out and replaced with water. This process is repeated two more times. What is the quantity of milk left in the vessel?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the replacement formula ‘Final Quantity = Initial × (1 - Replaced/Total)^n’. Here, multiplier = (1 - 10/100)^3 = (0.9)^3 = 0.729. Milk left = 100 × 0.729 = 72.9 L. Worked: After 1st operation: 100 × 9/10 = 90 L. After 2nd: 90 × 9/10 = 81 L. After 3rd: 81 × 9/10 = 72.9 L.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'LOGIC' is written as 'MNHJD'. Following the same pattern, how will 'RIGHT' be coded?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Observe the alternating pattern +1, -1 on alphabet positions: L(+1)→M, O(-1)→N, G(+1)→H, I(-1)→J, C(+1)→D. Apply to RIGHT: R(+1)→S, I(-1)→H, G(+1)→H, H(-1)→G, T(+1)→U → SHHGU. Full Solution: Write alphabets with positions. L(12)→M(13), O(15)→N(14), G(7)→H(8), I(9)→J(10), C(3)→D(4). Pattern confirmed as +1, -1 repeating. For R(18)→S(19), I(9)→H(8), G(7)→H(8), H(8)→G(7), T(20)→U(21). Coded word is SHHGU.

questions.text: A bag contains 5 red balls, 4 blue balls, and 3 green balls. If two balls are drawn at random, what is the probability that both balls are of the same colour?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use combination formula nCr. Favourable cases = 5C2 + 4C2 + 3C2 = 10+6+3 = 19. Total cases = 12C2 = 66. Probability = 19/66. Full Solution: Total balls = 12. Total ways to draw 2 balls = 12C2 = 66. Ways to draw 2 Red = 5C2 = 10. Ways to draw 2 Blue = 4C2 = 6. Ways to draw 2 Green = 3C2 = 3. Total favourable ways = 19. Required Probability = 19/66.

questions.text: Identify the missing word in the sentence: 'The _____ of the decision was delayed due to a lack of consensus among the members.' Options: A) Finality B) Annulment C) Postponement D) Implementation
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination): The sentence implies a delay in time. 'Finality' and 'Annulment' imply the end or cancellation, which contradicts 'delayed'. 'Implementation' is an action, not typically delayed by 'consensus' in this grammatical structure. Therefore, 'Postponement' is the only logical fit. Step-by-Step: The sentence describes a delay caused by lack of agreement. 'Finality' means the end; 'Annulment' means cancellation; 'Implementation' means putting into effect. 'Postponement' means delaying an event or action, which perfectly matches the context of being delayed due to consensus issues.

questions.text: As per the table below listing key Fiscal Reform Legislations in India and their years of enactment, the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act was enacted in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Table Lookup & Legislative Sequence Elimination. The table explicitly lists FRBM Act against 2003. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (2016) and GST Act (2017) are much later reforms. 2005 is a distractor (FRBM Rules notified). Step-by-step: 1. Locate 'FRBM Act' in the 'Legislation' column of the table. 2. Read the corresponding 'Year' value: 2003. 3. Verify distractors: 2016 (IBC), 2017 (GST) are subsequent major reforms. 4. Select 2003.

questions.text: Under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, what is the minimum number of workers ordinarily employed in an establishment for the mandatory provision of a crèche facility?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Memorize the OSH Code 'Welfare Threshold Ladder': Creche (50) → Canteen (100) → Welfare Officer (500). Eliminate Option A (30) as it was the threshold for women workers under the repealed Factories Act, 1948. Eliminate Option C (100) as it applies to Canteens. Option D (200) is a distractor. The correct threshold for Creche under the new Code is 50 workers. Step-by-Step: Section 67 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 mandates that every establishment wherein fifty or more workers are ordinarily employed must provide and maintain a crèche facility for the use of children of workers (aged 6 months to 6 years). This raised the threshold from the previous Factories Act requirement (30 women workers) and made it gender-neutral based on total workforce strength.
questions.topic: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 - Welfare Provisions

questions.text: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, an industrial establishment employing at least how many workers requires prior permission of the appropriate Government for lay-off, retrenchment, or closure?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The IR Code, 2020 uniformly raised the threshold for mandatory Standing Orders and prior Government permission for lay-off/retrenchment/closure from 100 (ID Act, 1947) to **300**. Eliminate 100 (old law), 500 (Welfare Officer threshold under OSH Code), and 200 (distractor). Worked Solution: Section 77 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 stipulates that the provisions relating to prior permission for lay-off, retrenchment, and closure apply to industrial establishments employing **300 or more workers** (previously 100 under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947).
questions.topic: Industrial Relations Code, 2020 - Lay-off, Retrenchment & Closure

questions.text: The 'Global Climate Action Summit' was recently held in California. Which Indian city was selected to host the next major climate conference organized under UNFCCC framework in 2024?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate based on capital status for international diplomatic events. Major UN events are typically held in the national capital. Step-by-step: New Delhi is the capital and hosted COP26 preparations and other major summits; Mumbai/Bengaluru/Chennai are unlikely for the primary host of a global UNFCCC conference.

questions.text: The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 governs the appointment process for the Election Commission of India. As per this Act, the Selection Committee for appointing the CEC and ECs consists of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and one other member. Who is the third member?

options.label: C
options.text: A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister

options.label: D
options.text: Senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court

questions.solution: Shortcut (Legislative History Trick): The Supreme Court's *Anoop Baranwal* judgment (March 2023) mandated a Committee of PM, LoP, and CJI. The Parliament passed the 2023 Act *specifically to overturn* the CJI's inclusion and restore executive primacy. Therefore, the CJI (Option A) is the distractor; the Act replaces CJI with a Cabinet Minister. Step-by-Step: Section 7 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 defines the Selection Committee. It comprises: (1) Prime Minister (Chairperson), (2) Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha (or leader of largest opposition party), and (3) A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The Act deliberately replaced the 'Chief Justice of India' (directed by the 2023 SC judgment) with a Cabinet Minister.

questions.text: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage change in the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Net % change in area = (L% + B% + (L% × B%)/100). Here, +20 + (-10) + (20 × -10)/100 = 10 - 2 = 8% increase. Step-by-step: Let original Length = L, Breadth = B. Original Area = L × B. New Length = 1.2L. New Breadth = 0.9B. New Area = 1.2L × 0.9B = 1.08 LB. Change in Area = 1.08LB - LB = 0.08LB. % Change = (0.08LB / LB) × 100 = 8%. Since positive, area increases by 8%.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error: The number of applicants for the post are unexpectedly high this year.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ignore the prepositional phrase 'of applicants'. The true subject is 'The number' (singular), requiring a singular verb 'is'. 'A number of' takes a plural verb, but 'The number of' takes a singular verb. Step-by-step: 1. Identify subject: 'The number'. 2. Note 'of applicants' is a modifier. 3. 'The number' is singular. 4. Verb 'are' is plural. 5. Error is in segment 'are'; correct form is 'is'.

questions.text: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how much time will the tank be filled?
questions.solution: Shortcut (LCM Method): Take LCM of 12, 15, 20 = 60 units (Tank Capacity). Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5 units/hr; B = 60/15 = 4 units/hr; C = -60/20 = -3 units/hr. Net Efficiency = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 units/hr. Time = 60/6 = 10 hours. Full Solution: Part filled by A in 1 hour = 1/12. Part filled by B in 1 hour = 1/15. Part emptied by C in 1 hour = 1/20. Net part filled in 1 hour = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10. Therefore, the tank will be filled in 10 hours.

questions.text: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, which of the following deductions from a worker's wages is expressly prohibited unless agreed to in writing by the workman?

options.label: B
options.text: Deduction for damage to machinery due to negligence

options.label: C
options.text: Deduction for non-payment of electricity bills in a factory

questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall that the Code on Wages strictly prohibits 'fines' unless agreed in writing, while deductions for damages or calamities have specific conditions. Eliminate options involving 'damage' (negligence usually allows deduction) and 'electricity bills'. The correct answer is fines without written agreement. Step-by-step: Section 76 of the Code lists prohibited deductions. Fines are only permissible with prior written consent. Damage to machinery can be deducted if due to negligence. National calamities are not a standard wage deduction category in this context. Therefore, option A is the correct prohibited action.

questions.text: The Goods and Services Tax (GST), India's biggest indirect tax reform subsuming multiple central and state taxes, was launched with effect from which date?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate April 1 (Fiscal Year start, missed deadline), January 1 (Calendar Year, not used for tax regime change), and October 2 (Gandhi Jayanti, symbolic only); the historic midnight parliamentary session launched GST on July 1, 2017. Full Solution: The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 paved the way for GST, which was officially rolled out across India on July 1, 2017, unifying the indirect tax structure.

questions.text: As per the Provisional Estimates of Annual National Income 2023-24 (released May 2024), the Real GDP growth rate for FY24 is estimated at 8.2%. If the Nominal GDP growth rate for the same period was approximately 9.6%, what is the approximate growth rate of the GDP Deflator (implicit price index)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: GDP Deflator Growth ≈ Nominal GDP Growth – Real GDP Growth. Calculation: 9.6% – 8.2% = 1.4%. This approximation holds because (1+Nominal) = (1+Real) × (1+Deflator) ≈ 1 + Real + Deflator for small rates. Full Solution: Nominal GDP = Real GDP × Price Index. Growth rates follow g_nom ≈ g_real + g_deflator. Substituting values: 9.6% ≈ 8.2% + g_deflator => g_deflator ≈ 1.4%.

questions.text: The Planning Commission of India (now replaced by NITI Aayog) was established by an executive resolution of the Government of India in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate 1947 (Independence) and 1949 (Constitution adoption) as the Commission was formed after the Constitution came into force. Eliminate 1951 as that marks the launch of the First Five Year Plan, which the Commission was created to formulate. Step-by-step: The Planning Commission was established by a Resolution of the Government of India on 15 March 1950, with the Prime Minister as its ex-officio Chairman, to assess the country's resources and formulate Five Year Plans.

questions.text: Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To burn the midnight oil'

options.label: A
options.text: To work late into the night

options.label: C
options.text: To light a lamp at midnight

options.label: D
options.text: To stay awake due to worry

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate literal meaning (Option C) and negative connotations (Option B). Option D is too specific (worry). The idiom originates from using oil lamps for studying/working late. Step-by-step: 1. Recognize historical context: oil lamps used for light. 2. 'Burning midnight oil' implies working/studying late. 3. Option A captures the essence of diligent late-night effort. 4. Options B, C, D are distractors (literal, negative, narrow).

questions.text: As per the table of Indian states' population (Census 2011), which state has the highest population density (people per sq km)? Table:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Among the listed states, Kerala is known for the highest density; recall that West Bengal's density is lower than Kerala's. Full solution: From Census 2011, Kerala's density is 860 persons/sq km, West Bengal 1,028, Bihar 1,102, Uttar Pradesh 828. Actually Bihar has the highest among these, but the table shows the values: Bihar 1,102 > West Bengal 1,028 > Kerala 860 > Uttar Pradesh 828. Hence the correct answer is Bihar (option index 1).

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks an article at ₹1,200. He offers two successive discounts of 20% and 15% respectively. What is the final selling price of the article?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Effective discount = 20% + 15% - (20×15)/100 = 32%. Selling price = (100-32)% of 1200 = 68% × 1200 = 816. Full: After 20% discount, price = 1200 × 0.8 = 960. After further 15% discount, price = 960 × 0.85 = 816.

questions.text: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 15 minutes. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many minutes will the empty tank be filled completely?
questions.solution: Shortcut (LCM Method): Take tank capacity as LCM(20, 30, 15) = 60 units. Efficiencies: A = +3 units/min, B = +2 units/min, C = -4 units/min. Net efficiency = +1 unit/min. Time = 60/1 = 60 minutes. Full Solution: Part filled by A in 1 min = 1/20, by B = 1/30. Part emptied by C in 1 min = 1/15. Net part filled in 1 min = 1/20 + 1/30 - 1/15 = (3+2-4)/60 = 1/60. Therefore, time required to fill the tank = 60 minutes.

questions.text: Kangchenjunga, the highest mountain peak located entirely within Indian territory and the third highest in the world, is situated in which state?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate K2/Godwin Austen (located in Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan, not Indian territory) and Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand, 2nd highest in India); Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak wholly within India, located in Sikkim. Worked Solution: Kangchenjunga lies on the border between Sikkim (India) and Nepal. Its main summit (8,586 m) is the highest point in India. K2 (8,611 m) is higher but lies in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan (administered by Pakistan). Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the second highest peak entirely within India, located in Uttarakhand.

questions.text: A property worth ₹10,00,000 is insured under two fire insurance policies: Policy A for ₹6,00,000 and Policy B for ₹4,00,000. A fire causes a loss of ₹3,00,000. Under the Principle of Contribution, what is the amount of claim payable by Policy A?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Claim = (Sum Insured under Policy / Total Sum Insured) × Actual Loss. Worked Solution: Total Sum Insured = ₹6,00,000 + ₹4,00,000 = ₹10,00,000. Since Total Sum Insured equals Property Value, Average Clause does not apply. Policy A's share = (6,00,000 / 10,00,000) × 3,00,000 = ₹1,80,000.

questions.text: As per the table below listing major Government of India Acts during British rule and their key constitutional features, which Act introduced 'Provincial Autonomy' by abolishing Dyarchy in the provinces?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Chronological Feature Elimination. The 1909 Act introduced Separate Electorates. The 1919 Act (Montagu-Chelmsford) introduced Dyarchy in provinces (referenced in seed data). The 1935 Act replaced Provincial Dyarchy with Provincial Autonomy. The 1947 Act granted Independence. Step-by-step: 1. Recall the sequence: 1909 (Electorates) -> 1919 (Dyarchy) -> 1935 (Autonomy) -> 1947 (Independence). 2. The question asks for the Act that *abolished* Dyarchy in provinces. 3. Since 1919 *introduced* Dyarchy, the next major Act (1935) removed it. 4. Select Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.text: Under Article 110 of the Constitution of India, the decision of which authority is final regarding the question of whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Executive heads (President, PM) and Judiciary (CJI) for a legislative classification power; certification of Money Bills is a exclusive privilege of the Lok Sabha Speaker. Full Solution: Article 110(3) explicitly states that if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the Speaker of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) thereon shall be final.

questions.text: As per AS 16 (Borrowing Costs), which of the following assets does **NOT** qualify as a 'Qualifying Asset' eligible for capitalization of borrowing costs?

options.label: A
options.text: Inventories that require a substantial period to bring them to a saleable condition

options.label: B
options.text: Manufacturing plants that require a substantial period of construction

options.label: C
options.text: Power generation facilities that require a substantial period of construction

options.label: D
options.text: Financial assets (e.g., investments in shares) held for trading purposes

questions.solution: **Shortcut/Trick:** Memorize the exclusion list: **Financial Assets (Shares, Bonds, Debentures) are NEVER Qualifying Assets**. Qualifying assets are strictly *physical/non-financial* assets (PPE, Investment Property, specific Inventories) taking substantial time to get ready. **Step-by-Step Solution:** 1. **Definition (AS 16 Para 5):** A Qualifying Asset is an asset that *necessarily takes a substantial period of time* to get ready for its intended use or sale. 2. **Standard Examples (Para 6):** Manufacturing plants, Power generation facilities, Inventories requiring substantial period (e.g., wine, timber), Investment Property under construction. 3. **Explicit Exclusions (Para 7):** Financial assets (investments in shares, debentures, etc.) and inventories produced in large quantities on a repetitive basis over a short period are **not** qualifying assets. 4. **Option Analysis:** - A: Qualifies (specific inventory taking time). - B: Qualifies (Plant under construction). - C: Qualifies (Power facility under construction). - D: **Correct Answer.** Financial assets held for trading are explicitly excluded from the definition of Qualifying Assets.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the Finance Commission constituted by the President?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options using known Article mappings. Article 356 deals with President's Rule (State Emergency), Article 324 deals with the Election Commission, and Article 243 deals with Panchayati Raj institutions. By elimination, Article 280 is the only remaining option for the Finance Commission. Worked Solution: Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year (or earlier) to recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and States and principles governing grants-in-aid.

questions.text: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act, 2023, enacted to strengthen the research ecosystem in India, provides for the subsumption of an existing statutory body responsible for promoting basic research in science and engineering. Which of the following bodies has been subsumed into the ANRF as per the Act?

options.label: A
options.text: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)

questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination by Mandate): ANRF is a funding/foundation body. CSIR, ICMR, and DRDO are massive, autonomous research *performing* establishments with distinct sectoral mandates (industrial, medical, defence). SERB was the primary *extramural funding agency* under DST for basic science/engineering grants, making it the logical entity to be merged into a new overarching National Research Foundation. Step-by-Step: The ANRF Act, 2023 (operationalized Feb 2024) establishes ANRF as the apex body for strategic direction of research. Section 25 of the Act explicitly states that the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB), established under the SERB Act, 2008, shall stand dissolved and its functions, assets, and liabilities transferred to ANRF. CSIR, ICMR, and DRDO continue to operate under their respective parent ministries/acts.

questions.text: The Cabinet Mission Plan, which proposed a united India with a federal structure and grouped provinces, arrived in India in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate 1942 (Cripps Mission), 1945 (Simla Conference/WWII end), and 1947 (Independence/Partition); 1946 is the only logical slot between the failed Simla Conference and the Mountbatten Plan. Full Solution: The Cabinet Mission, consisting of Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander, arrived in New Delhi on March 24, 1946, to discuss the transfer of power.

questions.text: Select the word which is nearest in meaning (SYNONYM) to the word given below: EPHEMERAL
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use etymology/root analysis. 'Ephemeral' derives from Greek 'epi' (on/around) + 'hemera' (day), meaning 'lasting only a day'. Instantly eliminate Options A, B, and D (Permanent, Eternal, Enduring) as they are antonyms denoting long duration. Option C (Temporary) is the only word signifying short duration. Worked Solution: Ephemeral means transitory or short-lived. Permanent means lasting indefinitely. Eternal means without beginning or end. Enduring means continuing long. Temporary means lasting for a limited time only. Therefore, Temporary is the correct synonym.

questions.text: If the cost price of an article is Rs. 800 and it is sold at a profit of 25%, what is the selling price? Use the shortcut of calculating 1/4th of the principal directly.
questions.solution: Shortcut: A 25% profit is equivalent to adding exactly one-fourth (1/4) of the cost price. Since 800 divided by 4 is 200, simply add 200 to 800 to get 1000. Full Solution: Selling Price = Cost Price + (Profit % * Cost Price)/100 = 800 + (25/100 * 800) = 800 + 200 = Rs. 1000.
